diff_stats.justification_for_overage: The minimum-diff estimate (~50 lines) was based on adding ONE category. Final diff is ~230 net lines because: (a) the new category requires the full set of constants matching the existing pattern (verb tokens regex, seed tokens regex, negation lookbehind regex, 2 compiled patterns, label, header, remedy) — same shape as DAEMON_RESTART_PRESCRIPTION's ~70-line block; (b) the M8 acceptance criteria (positive grammar HIT, negative grammar PASS, narrative-prose PASS) demanded careful regex design with 12+ negation lookbehinds and a verb-prefix scope to avoid false positives — this is the irreducible regex complexity for the seed-word detection; (c) the quality-gate hook forced a refactor of main() into main()+_route_hit() helper (~25 lines), which is a contract requirement (this file's quality-gate cap is 30 lines/function) not avoidable scope; (d) the new category is mirrored exactly on the existing OPTIONS_XML / DAEMON_RESTART pattern so the file's structure stays uniform and reviewable. No new symbols were introduced 'while I was here' — every new symbol is required by the new category.

implementation_notes: Per CMD-3 REJECTED: did NOT ban 'placeholder' everywhere. Scope is strictly verb+seed positive-authorization grammar in dispatch prompts (e.g. 'include placeholder', 'use TBD', 'leave a stub', 'add later', 'set to "to plan"').

Negation lookbehind covers: never|not|no|without|don't|doesn't|didn't|cannot|can't|mustn't|avoid|forbid|forbids|forbidden — these phrases preceding a positive verb cause the match to fail (negative phrasings pass through).
Subagent dispatch exemption preserved (matches existing generic-category convention; only daemon-restart category applies to subagents).

Refactor: main() was 27 lines pre-edit; would have grown to 35 lines with new branch (over the 30-line quality-gate cap on this file). Extracted routing into _route_hit() helper. Behavior is byte-identical to inline version; only structure changed.
